conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you during your stay. Can you tell me what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. I’ve been really sick the past two days—nauseous, throwing up, and constant diarrhea. I couldn’t keep anything down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Any fever, chills, or pain in your abdomen?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No fever or chills. My stomach doesn’t hurt, but I feel weak and dehydrated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. You’ve been on IV tigecycline for your left leg infection, right? That antibiotic can sometimes cause nausea and diarrhea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I’ve been on it for about six weeks. Could that really be causing this?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s possible. We’re going to pause the tigecycline for now and start you on oral vancomycin just in case it’s C. diff, but we suspect it’s a side effect.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So you think stopping the antibiotic will help?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and we’ll switch you to a different IV antibiotic that’s less likely to cause stomach issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs show your white count is elevated, but kidney function is stable. The diarrhea seems to be improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I haven’t vomited since last night, and the diarrhea is less frequent. That’s a relief.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. We’re going to start you on IV vancomycin and meropenem for your leg infection instead of tigecycline.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is my leg infection getting worse?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s still concerning. The vascular surgery team will see you today to evaluate the wound.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The vascular surgeon examined your left stump. They cleaned out the wound, but the infection has gone deep into the bone.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So what does that mean? More antibiotics?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Unfortunately, antibiotics alone won’t cure it. They recommend an above-knee amputation—AKA—to remove the infected bone.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Another amputation? I’m not sure I can handle that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. But if we don’t remove the infected part, the infection could spread and become life-threatening.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: How soon would I need the surgery?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: They suggest scheduling it within the next two weeks. In the meantime, we’ll start you on Bactrim by mouth to help control the infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m allergic to Bactrim, isn’t that dangerous?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see it’s listed in your allergies. We’ll avoid it and discuss alternatives with infectious disease.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I just need some time to process this surgery decision.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Of course. We’ll give you space and check back later. The team will support you through this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. We reviewed your urine test—there’s Klebsiella oxytoca, but it’s sensitive to several antibiotics, including meropenem, which you’re already on.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that why I had the UTI symptoms before?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly, but you’re not having symptoms now, so we’re covering it with your current antibiotics.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my PICC line—was it checked?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the chest X-ray showed it was out of position, so it was repositioned yesterday. It’s now in the right spot near your heart.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that why I felt discomfort in my chest?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly. It should feel better now. We’ll monitor it closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I spoke with infectious disease. Since you’re allergic to Bactrim, we’ll keep you on the IV antibiotics until surgery and adjust based on culture results.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my diabetes—has that been okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your sugars have been stable on your usual insulin—Lantus and Humalog. No changes needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’ve been worried about everything piling up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. You’ve been through a lot. But your nausea and diarrhea have resolved, your infection is being managed, and you’re making progress.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. We’re discharging you today. Continue your insulin, and take the oral vancomycin for a few more days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the surgery?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Call vascular surgery to schedule your AKA within the next two weeks. Keep taking your antibiotics and follow up with infectious disease for lab results.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And if I start feeling sick again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Call your doctor or go to the ER if you have fever, increased pain, drainage from the wound, or blood in your stool.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I’ll follow up on everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we’ll see you in follow-up.
